books.title: Magija, okultizmas ir krikščionybė – A.Menis
books.author: A.Menis
books.description: An exploration of magic, occultism, and their relationship to Christianity, with additional commentary on vampires and superstitions, featuring expert consultation by S.Rudalevičiūtė and V.Kapačauskas.

books.title: DVASINGUMAS IR SVEIKATA I
books.author: Arnoldas Eretas
books.description: A guide to duality and health covering topics such as nutrition, energy medicine, and natural healing practices. Part of the Sveikuolio Biblioteka (Health Library) series.

books.title: DVASINGUMAS IR SVEIKATA II
books.description: A religious educational text about duality and health, part of a spiritual library series focusing on salvation and evangelical teachings.

books.title: Kalbėk - až klausausi
books.author: Jaro Křivohlavý
books.description: A work by Jaro Křivohlavý exploring themes of communication and listening, published by Leidykla Jona in 1996.

books.title: ПСИХОТРЕНИНГ ПО МЕТОДУ ХОСЕ СИЛЬВЫ
books.author: Т. Пауэлл Дж. Пауэлл
books.description: A guide to the Jose Silva Method of psychotraining, presenting techniques for mental development and personal improvement through consciousness training.

books.title: KINU HOROSKOPAS
books.description: A diagnostic guide based on body meridians during the imperial period, combining horoscopic analysis with self-diagnosis methods according to the body's meridian systems.

books.title: VLADIMIRAS AZANOVAS AIŠKIAREGYSTĖS LABIRINTUOSE: reinkarnacija, poltergeistai, sveikata, magija, karma, meilė, Jaro...
books.author: Feliksas MARCINKAS
books.description: A book exploring the mystical labyrinth of Vladimir Azanov's clairvoyance, covering topics such as reincarnation, poltergeists, health, magic, karma, and love. Approved by Lithuanian journalists and edited by Vladimir Azanov.

books.title: KAIP įveikti stresą ir pradėti gyventi
books.author: DEILAS KARNEGIS
books.description: A guide on how to overcome stress and begin living better, based on principles of personal development and mental well-being.

books.title: DŪ TŪKSTANČIAI METŲ PO KRISTAUS IR ŽMONIJOS ATEITИСЬ
books.author: VYTAUTAS KAZLAUSKAS
books.description: A work by Vytautas Kazlauskas examining religious and philosophical themes related to two thousand years after Christ and humanity's future.

books.title: Jūsų pasąmonės galia
books.author: Joseph Murphy
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Joseph Murphy's work exploring the power of the subconscious mind and its influence on personal success and well-being. The book presents techniques for harnessing subconscious potential to achieve life goals.

books.title: MISTICZMAS
books.author: CARGO
books.description: A fantasy adventure novel featuring magical elements and mysterious characters. The book appears to be part of a series involving enchanted worlds and supernatural journeys.

books.title: ПОСЛЕДНИЙ ЗАВЕТ
books.description: A religious text featuring Orthodox Christian imagery with a cross at its center, likely a collection of biblical passages or religious teachings from the New Testament tradition.

books.title: Breakthrough in SAMATHA MEDITATION and VIPASSANĀ MEDITATION
books.author: Pa-auk Tawya Sayadaw and Dr. Mehm Tin Mon
books.description: Two papers on meditation presented at the World Buddhist Summit, explaining how Samatha-Vipassanā can be practiced as directed by the Buddha.

books.title: VIPPASSANA SPIRITUAL INSIGHT
books.author: SAYABAW
books.description: A discourse on Vipassana meditation and spiritual insight, translated by Dr. Ko Gyi. The book presents teachings on the venerable Maha Sayadaw's approach to Buddhist spiritual practice.

books.title: PURPOSE OF PRACTISING KAMMATTHANA MEDITATION
books.author: The Venerable Mahāsi Sayādaw of Myanmar
books.description: A guide to Kammatthana meditation practice by a respected Burmese Buddhist teacher, explaining the purposes and methods of this traditional meditation technique.

books.title: FUNDAMENTALS OF VIPASSANÂ MEDITATION
books.author: The Venerable Mahasi Sayadaw
books.description: A guide to Vipassanâ (insight) meditation techniques and practice as taught by the Venerable Mahasi Sayadaw, translated by Maung Tha Noe. The book provides foundational teachings on this Buddhist meditation method aimed at developing mindfulness and spiritual insight.

books.title: ОСВОБОЖДЕНИЕ
books.author: Дмитрий Верищагин
books.description: A system of further energoinformational development, first level. This book presents a methodology for personal development and consciousness expansion based on energoinformational principles.

books.title: SECOND SIGHT
books.author: DR. OOUR OF A SENSE MAVERICK—USE TODAY
books.description: An intuitive psychiatrist tells how to tap your own inner wisdom. The book explores how to develop and use your own intuitive psychic abilities for personal growth and decision-making.

books.title: PRACTICAL VIPASSANĀ MEDITATIONAL EXERCISE
books.author: MAHASI SAYADAW
books.description: A practical guide to vipassanā (insight) meditation exercises by the renowned Burmese Buddhist teacher Mahasi Sayadaw. The book provides instructions and techniques for practitioners seeking to develop mindfulness and insight through meditative practice.

books.title: ЦЕЛИТЕЛЬСТВО АКАДЕМИЧЕСКИЙ СЛОВАРЬ
books.description: An academic dictionary focused on healing and medical terminology, presented bilingually in Russian and English.

books.title: VIENUOLIO UŽRASAI
books.author: VYTAUTAS KAZLAUSKAS
books.description: A Lithuanian novel featuring a mysterious robed figure on the cover, suggesting themes of mysticism or spiritual exploration. The work appears to be a literary narrative exploring deeper philosophical or emotional dimensions.

books.title: Подводные камни в море биоэнергетики: о чем не говорят наставники Йоги и Ци-гун
books.author: Артур Омkaров
books.description: A critical examination of underwater pitfalls in bioenergetics, discussing what yoga and Qi-gung instructors don't tell their students about the practice of these disciplines.

books.title: ВИЗУАЛИЗАЦИЯ
books.author: Хелен Грэхэм
books.description: A practical manual on visualization techniques and methods. The book provides guidance on using mental imagery and visualization as a tool for personal development and achievement.

books.title: Dešimt vidinės ramybės ir sėkmės paslapčių
books.author: Wayne W. Dyer
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Wayne W. Dyer's work exploring ten secrets to inner peace and success. The book offers guidance on personal transformation and achieving both inner tranquility and external accomplishment.

books.title: ЭНЕРГЕТИЧЕСКОЕ ЗДОРОВЬЕ
books.author: М. Норбеков Ю. Хван
books.description: A book about energetic health and wellness practices, focusing on methods to improve personal vitality and well-being through various techniques and approaches.

books.title: Послания с небес
books.author: Учения Вознесенных Владык
books.description: A collection of surprising revelations about life after death and the future of Earth, presented as teachings from Ascended Masters.

books.title: КАК ЖИТЬ
books.author: Т.Н. ЗЮРНЯЕВА
books.description: A self-help guide by T.N. Zyurnyaeva offering philosophical and practical advice on how to live. Published by V.P. Ilyin publisher in Minsk.

books.title: Žmogus prasmės akivaizdoje
books.author: Viktor E. Frankl
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Viktor Frankl's work exploring human meaning and existence in the face of life's challenges. The book examines how individuals can find purpose and meaning in their lives.

books.title: DVAŠINES SAVIAUKLOS PATARIMAI
books.author: A.Menis, A.Blóom, C.S.Lewis
books.description: A guide offering practical advice and wisdom on personal self-improvement and life guidance, compiled from works by three authors.

books.title: DVASIU PASAULYJE
books.author: Stasė Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A Lithuanian literary work exploring themes of dual worlds or existence. The angelic imagery on the cover suggests spiritual or metaphysical dimensions to the narrative.

books.title: ЗАЩИТА ОТ СТРЕССА
books.author: Х. АЛМЕВ
books.description: A guide on how to protect oneself from stress and maintain well-being in modern conditions. The book provides practical advice for preserving and actualizing oneself in contemporary circumstances.

books.title: LIKIMO VALDYMO GALIMYBĖS TRANSERFINGAS
books.author: Vadim Zeland
books.description: A work exploring the possibilities of managing one's life and reality through the transerfing method, a concept developed by Vadim Zeland for personal development and consciousness expansion.

books.title: APLINKOS ENERGETIKA IR SVEIKATA. STEBUKLAI, ANTIKRITAS, REINKARNACIJA
books.author: A.Menis, S.Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A book exploring environmental energy and health, discussing miracles, anti-Christ themes, and reincarnation from a spiritual and metaphysical perspective.

books.title: MEILĖS SPALVOS
books.author: Clive Staples Lewis, Anthony Bloom, Aleksandr Men, Vladimir Solovjov, Nikolaj Berdjajev, Stasė Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A collection of essays exploring the nature and manifestations of love from philosophical and religious perspectives by various authors including C.S. Lewis and other notable thinkers.

books.title: Meilės ir neapykantos galios
books.author: Stasė Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A spiritual and philosophical work exploring themes of love, hate, energy, reincarnation, materialization, and karma through the S. Lazarev method. The book discusses soul energy, healing, and spiritual transformation.

books.title: KOSMITAI-TAI MES
books.author: STASĖ RUDALEVIČIŪTĖ
books.description: A Lithuanian science fiction novel exploring cosmic themes and humanity's place in the universe. The cover features surreal imagery combining ancient civilizations, space exploration, and mystical elements.

books.title: Moteriškumo ir vyriškumo dvasiniai pradai - pasakoja Stasė Rudalevičiūtė
books.author: Stasė Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A spiritual and philosophical exploration of femininity and masculinity, discussing their essential characteristics and spiritual dimensions.

books.title: GĖRIO IR BLOGIO TRAUKA
books.author: A.Men, C.S.Lewis, A.Bloom, N.Berdiajev, S.Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A collection of philosophical and spiritual essays exploring the nature of good and evil by renowned authors including C.S. Lewis and others, examining the human attraction to both moral and immoral forces.

books.title: KOSMITAI - TAI MES 2 dalis
books.author: S.Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A science fiction narrative set in a cosmic or space-themed environment, exploring themes of discovery and exploration across two parts.

books.title: Savęs bieškant-
books.author: Stasė Rudalevičiūtė
books.description: A reflective work exploring questions of aristocracy, bourgeoisie, and social class through the lens of temperament and character. The book presents tests and philosophical inquiries into identity and social status.

books.title: STIPRI NERVŲ SISTEMA—GYVENIMO PAGRINDAS
books.author: POLIS BREGAS
books.description: A book about the nervous system and its fundamental role in life, written by Polis Bregas. The work explores the biological foundations of the nervous system's function.

books.title: ЛОРА МНОГОУРОВНЕВАЯ СИСТЕМА САМООЗДОРОВЛЕНИЯ И ОМОЛОЖЕНИЯ ОРГАНИЗМА ЧЕЛОВЕКА
books.author: Лариса Фотина
books.description: A multi-level system for self-healing and rejuvenation of the human body. The book presents a comprehensive approach to health and wellness through various therapeutic techniques and methods.

books.title: МАЯТНИК ОТ БОЛЕЗНИ К ЗДОРОВЬЮ
books.author: Антон Штангел
books.description: A health and wellness guide discussing the path from illness to health, with focus on medical or therapeutic approaches to recovery and well-being.

books.title: LIKIMO VALDYMO GALIMYBĖS TRANSERIFINGAS I paruopa vartotojui erdė
books.author: Vaidin Zeland

books.title: Тренировка тела и духа
books.author: Миrzakarim Норбеков
books.description: A practical guide to training both body and mind through physical and spiritual exercises. The book provides techniques for improving health, vitality, and mental well-being.

books.title: Дневник слушателя учебно-оздоровительного курса
books.description: A diary for students of an educational and health improvement course, with an appendix referencing Mirzakarim Norbekov's book on healing through vision correction.

books.title: ТРАКТАТ О БЕЛОЙ МАГИИ
books.author: АЛИСА А.БЕЙЛИ
books.description: A treatise on white magic exploring spiritual and occult principles from a theosophical perspective. The work discusses magical practices and esoteric wisdom traditions.

books.title: KAIP ATSIKRATYTI NERIMO IR PRADĖTI GYVENTI
books.author: ALISA A.BEIJLI
books.description: A self-help book based on Dale Carnegie's principles about overcoming anxiety and starting to live. The subtitle indicates it focuses on proven methods for immediate relief from worry.

books.title: Valkirijos
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.description: A true-life spiritual odyssey in which Paulo Coelho and his wife embark on a forty-day journey into the Mojave Desert, encountering the Valkyries — warrior women on motorcycles — as Coelho seeks to communicate with his guardian angel and break a devastating curse. The book blends adventure, mysticism, and personal reflection on forgiveness and faith.

books.title: Piligrimas
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.description: A semi-autobiographical account of Paulo Coelho's 1986 pilgrimage along the ancient Road to Santiago de Compostela in Spain, guided by a mentor named Petrus. The journey becomes a profound meditation on self-discovery, fear, and spiritual transformation as Coelho seeks to reclaim a symbolic sword he failed to earn during a spiritual initiation.

books.title: Skaitymai minutėms
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.description: A thematically arranged collection of maxims, reflections, and thoughts drawn from Hermann Hesse's books and letters, compiled by editor Volker Michels. This Lithuanian edition was published by Trigrama in Kaunas.

books.title: DEMIANAS
books.author: HERMANAS HESĖ
books.description: A deeply introspective Bildungsroman following Emil Sinclair's journey from sheltered childhood through spiritual and psychological self-discovery, guided by the mysterious Max Demian. The novel explores the duality of human nature — light and darkness — drawing on Jungian psychology and Gnostic thought.

books.title: Vidurnakčio vaikai
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.description: A sweeping allegorical novel following Saleem Sinai, born at the exact midnight moment of India's independence on August 15, 1947, whose life becomes inextricably intertwined with the fate of his nation. He shares a telepathic connection with the other 'midnight's children,' all born in that first hour of independence and endowed with extraordinary gifts.

books.title: Brodekas
books.author: Philippe Claudel
books.description: A man named Brodeck is forced to write a report about the murder of a mysterious stranger in a small village in an unnamed country, in the aftermath of a devastating war. The novel is a haunting allegory about guilt, trauma, intolerance, and the darkness of human nature.

books.author: George Orwell
books.description: Set in a totalitarian future state called Oceania, the novel follows Winston Smith as he rebels against the all-controlling Party led by Big Brother. A landmark cautionary tale exploring surveillance, oppression, and the manipulation of truth and history.

books.title: Knyga apie San Mikelę
books.author: Axel Munthe
books.description: The Story of San Michele is the celebrated memoir by Swedish physician Axel Munthe, recounting his life as a fashionable doctor in Paris and his decades-long obsession with building a villa on the Isle of Capri on the ruins of Roman Emperor Tiberius's estate. First published in 1929, it became a worldwide bestseller translated into over 40 languages, blending autobiography, history, and vivid storytelling.

books.title: Šilkas
books.author: Alessandro Baricco
books.description: Set in 1861, the novel follows French silkworm merchant Hervé Joncour, who travels to Japan to smuggle silkworm eggs and becomes obsessed with a mysterious concubine whose eyes do not have an oriental slant. A lyrical, fable-like love story exploring desire, longing, and obsession.

books.title: NOVEČENTAS
books.author: Alessandro BARICCO
books.description: A theatrical monologue telling the story of a gifted pianist, Danny Boodmann T.D. Lemon Novecento, who was born and raised on a transatlantic ocean liner and never once set foot on land. His extraordinary musical talent captivates all who hear him, and the narrative explores themes of identity, belonging, and the transcendent power of music.

books.title: Pagiriamasis žodis kvailybei
books.author: Erazmas Roterdamietis
books.description: A satirical mock-encomium in which Folly herself praises her own virtues, poking fun at theologians, scholars, and the foibles of humanity. Originally written in Latin in 1509 and first published in 1511, it is Erasmus's most celebrated and enduring work.

books.title: Sofijos pasaulis
books.author: Jostein Gaarder
books.description: A novel following a young girl named Sophie who receives mysterious letters guiding her through the history of Western philosophy, exploring profound questions about existence and reality. This is the 1997 Lithuanian-language edition, translated from Norwegian by Eglė Išganaitytė.

books.title: Žmonijos priešai
books.author: Mika Waltari
books.description: Set in Rome during the turbulent early days of Christianity following the death of Christ, the novel follows Minutus, a Roman citizen navigating religion, politics, and survival. It is a sequel to The Secret of the Kingdom and the last major work Waltari published in his lifetime.

books.title: Motinos Pienas
books.author: Nora Ikstena
books.description: A novel following three generations of Latvian women living under Soviet rule, exploring the complex and fraught relationship between a mother and daughter through the recurring metaphor of mother's milk. Originally written in Latvian as Mātes piens, this is the Lithuanian translation published in Vilnius.

books.title: Brida
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.description: Brida follows a young Irish girl on a spiritual quest for knowledge and self-discovery, as she seeks guidance from wise mentors who introduce her to the traditions of magic. Her journey explores themes of love, destiny, and the search for one's soulmate.

books.title: Mirties Angelas
books.author: Mika Waltari
books.description: A historical novel set during the fall of Constantinople in 1453, told through the diary of John Angelos, a man torn between a hopeless love affair and his commitment to defend the dying Christian city against the Ottoman siege. This is a Lithuanian translation (from Finnish) by Aida Krilavičienė, published in Vilnius in 2008.

books.title: Stiklo Karoliukų Žaidimas
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.description: Set in a future utopian society, the novel follows Joseph Knecht's rise through the intellectual elite of Castalia, where he devotes himself to mastering the Glass Bead Game — a complex synthesis of music, mathematics, philosophy, and the arts. Hesse's final and most celebrated novel, it won him the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1946.

books.title: Laukinė Motina Gamta
books.author: Eglė Aukštakalnytė Hansen
books.description: A Lithuanian travel writer and photographer shares her extraordinary encounters with endangered and rare wildlife across the world's most remote wild places, from African rhinos and Komodo dragons to polar bears and mountain gorillas. The book is richly illustrated with the author's own nature photography and reflects on the urgent need to protect the natural world amid climate change.

books.title: 100 įtakingiausių asmenybių pasaulio istorijoje
books.author: Michael H. Hart
books.description: A ranking of the 100 people who most influenced human history, evaluated not by greatness but by the degree to which their actions changed the course of civilization. The book is a Lithuanian translation of Michael H. Hart's internationally bestselling work, originally published in 1978.

books.title: Sapiens: Glausta žmonijos istorija
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.description: A sweeping history of humankind, tracing the story of Homo sapiens from prehistoric times through the Cognitive, Agricultural, and Scientific Revolutions. Drawing on biology, anthropology, and economics, Harari examines how our species came to dominate the Earth and shaped the world we live in today.

books.title: Homo deus
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.description: Homo Deus explores the future of humanity, examining how humans have overcome famine, plague, and war, and now seek to upgrade themselves into gods using new technologies. Harari speculates on the directions our species might take in the centuries ahead, raising profound ethical and philosophical questions.

books.title: 21 pamoka XXI amžiui
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.description: A collection of provocative essays in which Yuval Noah Harari examines the most pressing issues of our time, from the rise of technology and artificial intelligence to nationalism, religion, and the challenges facing liberal democracy in the 21st century.

books.title: Pompėjai
books.author: Mary Beard
books.description: A richly detailed portrait of everyday life in the ancient Roman city of Pompeii, whose ruins were preserved after the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE. Mary Beard interprets archaeological evidence to explore topics ranging from street life and trade to food, religion, and sex, while challenging many long-held myths about the city.

books.title: Milijonas metų per vieną dieną
books.author: Greg Jenner
books.description: Structured around one ordinary day, this book traces the astonishing origins and development of daily routines we take for granted, spanning a million years of human history. It is the Lithuanian translation of Greg Jenner's 'A Million Years in a Day', published by Alma littera in Vilnius.

books.title: Išsamus fotografijos kursas
books.author: John Garrett ir Graeme Harris
books.description: A practical, project-based photography course covering everything from basic composition to digital darkroom techniques, suitable for all skill levels. Originally published in English as 'Collins Complete Photography Course', this is the Lithuanian translation.

books.title: Kaip prižiūrėti katę
books.author: Andrew Edney, David Taylor
books.description: A Lithuanian-language edition of the '101 Essential Tips: Cat Care' guide by Dorling Kindersley, covering practical advice on choosing, feeding, grooming, training, and caring for cats. Published by Alma Littera in Vilnius in 1997.

books.title: 1000 TIESOS AKIBROKŠTŲ
books.author: Christa Poppelmann
books.description: A Lithuanian-language edition of Christa Poppelmann's work debunking 1,000 widely held misconceptions and myths across various fields of knowledge. Originally published in German, it covers topics ranging from science and history to culture and religion.

books.title: Laimingasis
books.author: Juozas Grušas
books.description: A collected volume of dramas, short stories, and novellas by the prominent Lithuanian writer and playwright Juozas Grušas (1901–1986), published as part of the series 'Lietuvių literatūros lobynas. XX amžius' (Treasury of Lithuanian Literature: 20th Century). Grušas's work is known for its moral and existential themes, paradox-driven style, and a blend of tragedy and tragicomedy.

books.title: Sodybų tuštėjimo metas
books.author: Jonas Avyžius
books.description: A major Lithuanian novel set against the backdrop of foreign occupation and Soviet-era Lithuania, exploring the existential struggles of the Lithuanian intelligentsia and nation. The work portrays characters forced to choose between collaboration, resistance, and withdrawal amid sweeping historical upheaval.

books.title: Miškais ateina ruduo
books.author: Marius Katiliškis
books.description: A psychological novel set in a forest-surrounded Lithuanian village on the eve of World War II, exploring themes of human fate, love, and the deep connection between people and nature. Some critics consider it the finest prose work ever written in Lithuanian.

books.title: Ir rados stebuklas
books.author: Jonas Biliūnas
books.description: A collection of short stories, a novella, and literary criticism by Jonas Biliūnas (1879–1907), one of the most significant early Lithuanian prose writers, known for his lyrical, empathetic portrayals of rural Lithuanian life and the human condition. Published as part of the "Lietuvių literatūros lobynas" (Lithuanian Literature Treasury) series by Lietuvos rašytojų sąjungos leidykla, Vilnius.

books.title: Aukso sapnas
books.author: Šatrijos Ragana
books.description: A prose anthology by Šatrijos Ragana (Marija Pečkauskaitė, 1877–1930), one of the most significant Lithuanian prose writers, known for her impressionistic style. The collection includes works considered enduring classics of Lithuanian literature, among them the semi-autobiographical novella 'Sename dvare.'

books.title: Grįžo
books.author: Antanas Vienuolis
books.description: A collection of short stories, novellas, and legends by one of Lithuania's most celebrated classic writers, Antanas Vienuolis, exploring themes of human psychology, rural life, and the conflict of the individual with society. This edition, published without Soviet-era distortions, draws primarily from pre-war publications.

books.title: Pas Dangaus Vartus
books.author: Vincas Krėvė
books.description: A collection of prose and drama by one of Lithuania's most prominent 20th-century writers, Vincas Krėvė, featuring works set in the Dzūkija countryside and exploring themes of faith, folk worldview, and human existence. The volume also includes the historical drama Skirgaila, considered a cornerstone of Lithuanian national dramatic literature.

books.title: KAS BUVO IR KAS YRA
books.author: JUOZAS TUMAS-VAIŽGANTAS
books.description: A selected prose anthology of Juozas Tumas-Vaižgantas, one of Lithuania's most celebrated writers and Catholic priests, whose fiction masterfully blends realist narrative with romantic vision, depicting Lithuanian national life, rural folk, and the cultural awakening of his era. Published as the 28th volume in the series 'Lietuvių literatūros lobynas. XX amžius' by Lietuvos rašytojų sąjungos leidykla, Vilnius.

books.title: Žingsniai ir laiptai
books.author: Antanas Škėma
books.description: A representative anthology of Lithuanian modernist writer Antanas Škėma (1910–1961), collecting cycles of short stories, a novel, and dramas. The work is considered a symbolic portrayal of an exodus situation and a drama of human existence, written by an author often called the 'Lithuanian Albert Camus.'

books.title: Man vėtra sesuo
books.author: Kazys Boruta
books.description: A collection of prose and poetry by Lithuanian writer Kazys Boruta (1905–1965), featuring his celebrated novels including the first edition of *Baltaragio malūnas* and *Mediniai stebuklai*, alongside selected poems showcasing his rebellious, storm-spirited literary voice. Published as the 26th volume in the series *Lietuvių literatūros lobynas. XX amžius* (Lithuanian Literature Treasury: 20th Century).

books.title: Sakmė apie Juzą
books.author: Juozas Baltušis
books.description: A Lithuanian novel following Juza, a hermit who voluntarily lives in seclusion in a marsh, only to find it impossible to hide from the sweeping cataclysms of the world — genocide, war, and upheaval. Considered Baltušis's finest work, it won the Lithuanian SSR State Prize in 1980 and the prestigious French Prix du Meilleur Livre Étranger in 1990.

books.title: Rytą Giedra
books.author: Žemaitė
books.description: A collection featuring Žemaitė's unfinished autobiography, in which she recounts her life against a broad social backdrop, alongside her celebrated short stories depicting the everyday life of Lithuanian peasants with realism and compassion. Žemaitė (1845–1921) was one of Lithuania's most prominent writers and a key figure in the Lithuanian National Revival.

books.title: Moderniškas Pavasaris
books.author: Kazys Binkis
books.description: A selected works anthology of Kazys Binkis (1893–1942), the pioneer of Lithuanian avant-garde literature, featuring his innovative poetry collection '100 Pavasarių' and other poems, as well as dramas including 'Atžalynas' and 'Generalinė repeticija'. Published as the 23rd volume in the 'Lietuvių literatūros lobynas. XX amžius' (Lithuanian Literary Treasury: 20th Century) series by Lietuvos rašytojų sąjungos leidykla, Vilnius.

books.title: Graži tu mano
books.author: Maironis
books.description: A collection of lyric poetry and an epic poem by Maironis (Jonas Mačiulis, 1862–1932), the celebrated bard of the Lithuanian National Revival, featuring the final 1927 version of his iconic 'Pavasario balsai' (Voices of Spring) and the renowned poem 'Jaunoji Lietuva' (Young Lithuania). Published by Lietuvos rašytojų sąjungos leidykla in Vilnius to mark the 150th anniversary of the poet's birth.

books.title: Visi eilėraščiai
books.author: Henrikas Radauskas
books.description: A comprehensive collection of all published poems by Henrikas Radauskas (1910–1970), one of the most celebrated Lithuanian lyric poets, known for his aestheticism and poetic transformation of reality. First published in 2007 by Lietuvos rašytojų sąjungos leidykla (Lithuanian Writers' Union Publishing House) in Vilnius, as part of the series "Lietuvių literatūros lobynas. XX amžius" (Lithuanian Literary Treasury. 20th Century).

books.title: CHIMEROS AKYS
books.author: JONAS AISTIS
books.description: A selected poetry collection (poezijos rinktinė) by Jonas Aistis (1904–1973), one of Lithuania's most celebrated neoromantic lyric poets, published by Lietuvos Rašytojų Sąjungos Leidykla in Vilnius. The collection draws from Aistis's deeply personal, elegiac verse, characterized by the tension between ideal and reality, intimate emotional expression, and themes of longing and homeland.

books.title: Meilužis
books.author: Marguerite Duras
books.description: A semi-autobiographical novel set in French colonial Indochina, recounting a passionate and clandestine affair between a young French adolescent girl and a wealthy older Chinese man. It won the Prix Goncourt in 1984 and has been translated into 43 languages.

books.title: Triukšmas ir įniršis
books.author: William Faulkner
books.description: A landmark modernist novel that chronicles the decline and disintegration of the aristocratic Compson family in the American South, told through the interior monologues of three brothers and a fourth-person narrator. First published in 1929, this Lithuanian edition (translated by Violeta Tauragienė) is renowned for its innovative stream-of-consciousness technique and nonlinear narrative structure.

books.title: Žvaigždės spindi danguje
books.author: SIDNEY SHELDON
books.description: The story of Lara Cameron, a self-made billionaire and real estate tycoon who rises from a troubled past to build a glamorous business empire, only to find her fortune, fame, and love suddenly and shockingly imperiled. Originally published in English in 1992, this is the Lithuanian translation by Laima Račienė.

books.title: Prisukamas apelsinas
books.author: Anthony Burgess
books.description: A Clockwork Orange follows Alex, a teenage gang leader in a near-future dystopian society, who narrates his violent exploits in an invented slang called Nadsat. After being imprisoned and subjected to state-sponsored psychological conditioning, the novel raises profound questions about free will, morality, and the ethics of behavior modification.

books.title: Aušros pažadas
books.author: Romain Gary
books.description: A semi-autobiographical account in which Romain Gary recounts his childhood in Eastern Europe and his adventurous path to becoming a WWII pilot, diplomat, and celebrated French writer, all shaped by his mother's fierce, unconditional ambition for him. Originally published in French as 'La promesse de l'aube' in 1960, this Lithuanian edition was translated by Violeta Tauragienė.

books.title: Stepių vilkas
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.description: Steppenwolf follows Harry Haller, a middle-aged intellectual who sees himself as torn between human and wolf natures, alienated from bourgeois society. The novel explores themes of identity, duality, and the struggle between the spiritual and the mundane.

books.title: Kelias į Indiją
books.author: Edward Morgan Forster
books.description: Set during the British Raj in 1920s India, the novel explores the cultural tensions and misunderstandings between British colonizers and Indian people, centering on a controversial incident involving an English woman and an Indian doctor. It is widely regarded as a masterpiece of 20th-century literature examining colonialism, racism, and the barriers to cross-cultural friendship.

books.title: Plačiai užmerktos akys
books.author: ARTHUR SCHNITZLER
books.description: A 1926 novella set in turn-of-the-century Vienna, following a married doctor whose wife's confession of a fantasy sends him on a dreamlike, erotically charged nocturnal adventure through masked balls and secret societies. It served as the basis for Stanley Kubrick's 1999 film Eyes Wide Shut.

books.title: Žodžiai
books.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
books.description: Les Mots (The Words) is Jean-Paul Sartre's 1964 autobiography recounting his childhood and the origins of his vocation as a writer. Divided into two parts — 'Reading' and 'Writing' — it reflects on how he constructed his identity through language and literature, while critically examining his bourgeois upbringing.

books.title: Aš ateisiu nusispjauti ant jūsų kapų
books.author: Boris Vian
books.description: Originally published in French in 1946 under the pseudonym Vernon Sullivan, this provocative noir novel follows a light-skinned Black man who infiltrates a small Southern American town to exact violent revenge for his brother's lynching. The book caused a scandal in France and was later revealed to have been written by Vian himself.

books.title: Amerika (Pražuvėlis) / Laiškas tėvui
books.author: Franz Kafka
books.description: This Lithuanian volume combines two of Kafka's major works: Amerika (Pražuvėlis) — his unfinished first novel about young Karl Rossmann, banished to America by his parents and swept into strange picaresque misadventures — and Laiškas tėvui (Letter to His Father), Kafka's deeply personal 1919 letter examining his lifelong fear of his domineering father and the psychological toll of their fraught relationship.

books.title: Iš Afrikos
books.author: Karen Blixen
books.description: A memoir recounting Danish author Karen Blixen's seventeen years living in Kenya, where she managed a coffee plantation and formed deep bonds with the land and its people. Originally published in English in 1937, this is the Lithuanian translation by Violeta Tauragienė.

books.title: Ledi Čaterli meilužis
books.author: David Herbert Lawrence
books.description: A novel following Lady Constance Chatterley, trapped in a passionless marriage to her paralyzed aristocratic husband, who embarks on a passionate affair with his gamekeeper, Oliver Mellors. First published in 1928, it was famously banned in England and the United States for its explicit content.

books.title: Pornografija
books.author: Witold Gombrowicz
books.description: Set in Nazi-occupied Poland during World War II, the novel follows two middle-aged Warsaw intellectuals who travel to a countryside manor and become obsessively fixated on two young locals, ultimately drawing them into a dark scheme of manipulation and violence. Originally published in Polish in 1960, this is a Lithuanian translation by Skirmantė Kristina Ramanauskaitė, published by Lietuvos rytas.

books.title: Moteris smėlynuose
books.author: Kobo Abe
books.description: An amateur entomologist on a seaside trip finds himself trapped at the bottom of a vast sand pit with a young woman, forced to endlessly shovel back the encroaching dunes that threaten to bury their village. This acclaimed existential novel explores themes of identity, freedom, and the human condition.

books.title: Vakarų fronte nieko naujo
books.author: Erich Maria Remarque
books.description: Told through the eyes of young German soldier Paul Bäumer, the novel depicts the brutal realities of trench warfare during World War I. A landmark of anti-war literature, it explores themes of disillusionment, survival, and the psychological trauma inflicted on a generation of young men.

books.title: Šuns Širdis
books.author: Michail Bulgakov
books.description: A satirical novella in which a Moscow surgeon transplants human organs into a stray dog, transforming it into a vulgar, bureaucratic man — a sharp critique of Soviet social engineering and the ideals of the October Revolution. Written in 1925, it was banned in the Soviet Union for decades.

books.title: Karo šunys
books.author: Frederick Forsyth
books.description: A British industrialist discovers a vast platinum deposit in a fictional African country and hires a team of mercenaries to overthrow its despotic ruler. The novel meticulously details the planning, recruitment, and logistics of the coup attempt.

books.title: Badas Panas Viktorija
books.author: Knut Hamsun
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection of three celebrated novels by Nobel Prize-winning Norwegian author Knut Hamsun: Hunger (Badas), Pan (Panas), and Victoria (Viktorija). The works explore themes of starvation and the human psyche, untamed nature and doomed love, and romantic longing, translated from German by Vytautas Petrauskas.

books.title: Pavadinimas
books.author: Juozas Erlickas
books.description: A selected anthology of works by Lithuanian humorist Juozas Erlickas, featuring prose, poetry, and plays infused with absurdist black humor and sharp irony. The collection satirizes Lithuanian social and political life, blending parody and dark comedy in the author's signature style.

books.title: Apakimas
books.author: Elias Canetti
books.description: A novel following Peter Kien, a reclusive sinologist who lives among his vast private library, as he descends into madness. Originally published in German as *Die Blendung* (1935), it explores isolation, intellectualism, and destruction.

books.title: Iš Afrikos
books.author: KAREN BLIXEN
books.description: A lyrical memoir recounting Karen Blixen's eighteen years living on a coffee plantation in Kenya, then British East Africa. It reflects on her deep bond with the African landscape, its people, and her love for adventurer Denys Finch-Hatton.

books.title: Tykusis amerikietis
books.author: Graham Greene
books.description: Set during the First Indochina War, the novel follows British journalist Thomas Fowler and his entanglement with idealistic American operative Alden Pyle, exploring themes of colonialism, moral ambiguity, and the consequences of Western interventionism in Vietnam.

books.title: Dievų miškas
books.author: Balys Sruoga
books.description: A memoir by Lithuanian writer Balys Sruoga recounting his experiences as a prisoner in the Nazi Stutthof concentration camp, to which he was deported in March 1943 along with dozens of other Lithuanian intellectuals. The work is notable for its use of dark irony and sardonic humor as a means of coping with and depicting the brutal realities of camp life.

books.title: Antikiniai Romanai ir Pasakėčios
books.author: Longas, Petronijus, Apulėjus, Ezopas, Fedras
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology of ancient Greek and Roman prose, including Longus's 'Daphnis and Chloe,' Petronius's 'Satyricon,' and Apuleius's 'The Golden Ass,' alongside selected fables by Aesop and Phaedrus, translated from ancient Greek and Latin.

books.title: KALEVALA
books.author: JUSTINAS MARCINKEVIČIUS
books.description: The Kalevala is the Finnish national epic, compiled by Elias Lönnrot from oral folk songs and mythology, telling of the world's creation and legendary heroes such as Väinämöinen. This is the Lithuanian translation by poet Justinas Marcinkevičius, published in Vilnius in 1986 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Badas. Panas
books.author: Knutas Hamsunas
books.description: This Lithuanian-language volume contains two early novels by Knut Hamsun: *Badas* (*Hunger*), a semi-autobiographical portrait of a starving intellectual's psychological and physical deterioration, and *Panas* (*Pan*), a lyrical story of a lieutenant who retreats into the solitude of nature and becomes entangled in a passionate and ill-fated love. Published by Vaga, Vilnius, 1987, as part of the *Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka* (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Apysakos Apsakymai
books.author: Džozefas Konradas, Radjardas Kiplingas
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology collecting novellas and short stories by Joseph Conrad and Rudyard Kipling, published as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series by Vaga in Vilnius.

books.title: ENEIDA
books.author: Vergilijus
books.description: The Aeneid is a Latin epic poem by Virgil following Aeneas, a Trojan hero who escapes the fall of Troy and journeys across the Mediterranean, destined by fate to found the kingdom that will become Rome. This 1989 Lithuanian edition, published in Vilnius as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series, was translated from Latin by Antanas Dambrauskas.

books.title: Džozefo Endriuso ir jo draugo pono Abrahamo Adamso nuotykių istorija,
books.author: Henris Fildingas
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Henry Fielding's 1742 comic novel following the virtuous young footman Joseph Andrews and his companion Parson Adams on a picaresque journey from London back to the countryside, filled with misadventures, social satire, and commentary on hypocrisy and virtue. The title page notes it was written in the style of Cervantes, the author of Don Quixote.

books.title: Apysakos
books.author: Šolom Aleichemas
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection of short stories by Sholem Aleichem, translated from Yiddish by Dominykas Urbas, published as part of the prestigious Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (Library of World Literature) series. The stories depict humorous and poignant scenes of Jewish life in Eastern Europe.

books.title: Apsakymai Apysakos
books.author: Ivanas Buninas, Aleksandras Kuprinas
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology collecting short stories and novellas by two celebrated Russian writers, Ivan Bunin and Alexander Kuprin, published as part of the 'Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka' (World Literature Library) series in Vilnius. Both authors were prominent figures in early 20th-century Russian realism, renowned for their richly crafted prose.

books.title: Motina Artamonovai
books.author: Maksimas Gorkis
books.description: A multigenerational family saga tracing the rise and fall of the Artamonov family, who found a linen factory in post-Emancipation Russia and amass wealth over three generations, only to decline as revolutionary forces reshape society leading up to 1917. Published in Vilnius as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Tykusis Donas 2
books.author: Michailas Šolochovas
books.description: A sweeping epic novel following Cossack Grigory Melekhov and his community along the Don River through WWI, the Russian Revolution, and the Civil War. It explores love, loyalty, and moral ambiguity against the backdrop of Russia's most turbulent historical upheavals.

books.title: Broliai
books.author: Terencijus
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of the Roman playwright Terence's Adelphoe (The Brothers), a verse comedy first performed in 160 BC exploring contrasting approaches to raising children. The play is considered Terence's masterpiece and examines themes of parenting, freedom, and human nature.

books.title: Amfitrionas
books.author: PLAUTAS
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Plautus's ancient Roman comedy *Amphitryon* (c. 185 BCE), in which Jupiter disguises himself as the Theban general Amphitryon to seduce his wife Alcmena, leading to a series of comic misunderstandings involving mistaken identity and divine trickery. Published in the *Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka* (World Literature Library) series by Vaga, Vilnius, 1989.

books.title: Dvyniai
books.author: PLAUTAS
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Plautus's Roman comedy Menaechmi, about twin brothers separated in childhood who are reunited after a series of hilarious cases of mistaken identity. The play, which inspired Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors, was published in Vilnius by Vaga as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Karys pagyrūnas
books.author: Plautas
books.description: A Roman comedy (originally Miles Gloriosus) by Plautus, in which a vainglorious braggart soldier is outwitted by a clever slave and a courtesan who conspire to free a captive girl and reunite her with her true lover. This is the Lithuanian translation included in the anthology Antikinės komedijos, published by Vaga in Vilnius.

books.title: Vergas apgavikas
books.author: PLAUTAS
books.description: A Roman comedy in which the clever slave Pseudolus schemes to help his young master Calidorus win back his beloved Phoenicium, who has been sold to a Macedonian soldier, by outwitting a conniving pimp and deceiving those around him. This is the Lithuanian translation of Plautus's Pseudolus, published as part of the anthology Antikinės komedijos by Vaga (Vilnius, 1989).

books.title: Bambeklis
books.author: Menandras
books.description: Bambeklis (Dyskolos, or "The Grouch") is the only nearly complete surviving comedy by the ancient Greek playwright Menander, following a misanthropic old farmer named Knemon and a young man's efforts to win his daughter's hand in marriage. This Lithuanian edition, translated by Jonas Dumčius, was published in 1989 as part of the "Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka" (World Literature Library) anthology of ancient comedies.

books.title: Plutas
books.author: Aristofanas
books.description: Plutas (Plutus) is Aristophanes' last surviving comedic play, first produced in 388 BC, in which an Athenian farmer named Chremylos encounters Plutus, the blind god of wealth, and schemes to restore his sight — satirizing the unequal distribution of wealth and power in Athenian society.

books.title: Varlės
books.author: Aristofanas
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Aristophanes' ancient Greek comedy *The Frogs* (405 BC), in which the god Dionysus descends to the underworld to bring back a great tragic poet to save Athenian theater. The play culminates in a literary contest between Aeschylus and Euripides, making it one of the earliest works of literary criticism in Western tradition.

books.title: Taika
books.author: ARISTOFANAS
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Aristophanes' ancient Greek comedy Peace (421 BCE), in which a farmer named Trygaeus rides a dung beetle to the heavens to free the goddess of peace from her cave. The play was written to urge an end to the Peloponnesian War and joyously anticipates a return to peaceful rural life.

books.title: Debesys
books.author: Aristofanas
books.description: A comedic play by the ancient Greek playwright Aristophanes in which the debt-ridden Strepsiades attempts to learn sophistry from a satirically portrayed Socrates in order to outwit his creditors, with disastrous results. The play is a sharp satire of intellectual pretension and the conflict between traditional and new values in Athenian society.

books.title: ANTIKINĖS KOMEDIJOS
books.author: ARISTOFANAS, MENANDRAS, PLAUTAS, TERENCIJUS
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology of comedies by the greatest ancient playwrights — Greek writers Aristophanes and Menander, and Roman writers Plautus and Terence — published as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series. The collection includes works translated into Lithuanian, showcasing the wit, satire, and humanism of classical antiquity.

books.title: XX a. Rytų Proza
books.author: Lu Sinis, Lao Šė, Riunoskė Akutagava, Jasunaris Kavabata
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology of 20th-century Eastern prose, part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series, featuring works by Chinese authors Lu Xun and Lao She and Japanese authors Ryūnosuke Akutagawa and Yasunari Kawabata. Published in Vilnius in 1986, it brings together landmark works of modern Asian literature in translation.

books.title: Geismų tramvajus
books.author: Tenesis Viljamsas
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Tennessee Williams's Pulitzer Prize-winning play A Streetcar Named Desire, subtitled 'a play in eleven scenes.' It follows the faded Southern belle Blanche DuBois as she moves in with her sister in New Orleans and clashes violently with her brutish brother-in-law Stanley Kowalski.

books.title: Elektrai skirta gedėti
books.author: Judžinas O'Nilas
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Eugene O'Neill's 1931 trilogy *Mourning Becomes Electra*, a modernized retelling of Aeschylus's Oresteia set in post-Civil War New England, exploring themes of fate, revenge, and psychological conflict within the Mannon family.

books.title: NEPALAIDOTI MIRUSIEJI
books.author: Žanas Polis Sartras
books.description: A four-act play set during World War II and the French Resistance movement, in which a group of partisans captured after a failed operation face physical and psychological torture. The play explores existentialist themes of fear, choice, and human resilience in extreme, borderline situations.

books.title: HENRIKAS IV
books.author: Luidžis Pirandelas
books.description: A three-act tragedy in which an Italian nobleman falls from his horse during a carnival pageant and comes to believe he is Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor. For twenty years those around him maintain an elaborate charade to sustain his delusion, while the play explores themes of madness, identity, and the nature of reality.

books.title: GERAS ŽMOGUS IŠ SEZUANO
books.author: Bertoltas Brechtas
books.description: An allegorical parable play in which three gods descend to a Chinese city searching for a good person, and give a kind-hearted young woman money to start a new life, forcing her to wrestle with the impossible tension between goodness and survival in a harsh, exploitative world. This is the Lithuanian translation of Bertolt Brecht's Der gute Mensch von Sezuan.

books.title: Orfėjas
books.author: Žanas Kokto
books.description: A surrealist one-act play by Jean Cocteau that reimagines the ancient Greek myth of Orpheus, blending the legendary poet's descent into the Underworld to retrieve Eurydice with modern, fantastical stagecraft and anachronistic dialogue. First performed in Paris in 1926, it is considered one of Cocteau's masterworks.

books.title: XX a. Vakarų Dramos
books.description: An anthology collecting the most significant works of prominent 20th-century Western playwrights, including J. Cocteau, B. Brecht, L. Pirandello, J.M. Synge, J.-P. Sartre, E. O'Neill, and T. Williams. Published as part of the Lithuanian "Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka" (World Literature Library) series by Vaga publishing house.

books.title: Kinų poezija
books.description: An anthology of Chinese poetry translated into Lithuanian, published as part of the 'Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka' (World Literature Library) series by the Lithuanian publisher Vaga. The collection presents selections from classical and/or traditional Chinese verse for Lithuanian readers. Senoves rytų poezija

books.title: Senovės Iranėnų Poezija
books.description: A section of the Lithuanian anthology Senovės Rytų poezija (Ancient Eastern Poetry), compiled by Sigitas Geda, this chapter presents ancient Iranian (Persian/Avestan) poetry translated into Lithuanian. The broader anthology collects ancient world poetry from civilizations including Egypt, Mesopotamia, India, and Iran.

books.title: Senovės Indijos Poezija
books.description: A section of the Lithuanian anthology 'Senovės Rytų poezija' (Ancient Eastern Poetry), compiled by Sigitas Geda, featuring ancient Indian literary monuments spanning various genres that reflect the worldview and culture of ancient peoples. Senoves rytų poezija

books.title: Senovės žydų poezija
books.description: A section within the Lithuanian anthology 'Senovės Rytų poezija' (Ancient Eastern Poetry), compiled by Sigitas Geda, collecting ancient Jewish poetry as part of the World Literature Library series. The volume gathers early poetic monuments reflecting the worldview and culture of ancient peoples. Senoves rytų poezija

books.title: Senovės Rytų poezija
books.author: sudarė Sigitas Geda
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology of ancient world poetry spanning from the 27th–24th centuries BCE, including works from Egyptian, Sumerian, Babylonian, Hittite, ancient Jewish, ancient Indian, Chinese, and Japanese literary traditions. The collection reflects the worldview and culture of ancient peoples across a variety of poetic genres. Senoves rytų poezija.

books.title: HETITŲ POEZIJA
books.author: Sigitas Geda
books.description: A section of Hittite sacred poetry appearing in the Lithuanian anthology Senovės Rytų poezija (Ancient Eastern Poetry), compiled and translated by Lithuanian poet Sigitas Geda. The anthology brings together masterpieces of ancient Near Eastern poetry — including Sumerian hymns, the Gilgamesh Epic, Hittite texts, and the Song of Songs — translated into Lithuanian. Senoves rytų poezija.

books.title: BABILONIEČIŲ POEZIJA
books.author: Sigitas Geda
books.description: A section of the Lithuanian anthology Senovės Rytų poezija (Ancient Eastern Poetry), compiled and translated by Sigitas Geda, featuring Babylonian poetry rendered into Lithuanian. The broader anthology, published by Vaga in 1991, brings together poetic masterworks of the ancient Near East including Sumerian hymns, the Epic of Gilgamesh, and Babylonian verse. Senoves rytų poezija

books.title: ŠUMERO POEZIJA
books.description: A section of Sumerian poetry from the Lithuanian anthology Senovės Rytų poezija (Ancient Eastern Poetry), compiled by Sigitas Geda and published by Vaga in 1991. The anthology gathers ancient world poetry dating from the 27th–24th centuries BCE, including Egyptian, Sumerian, Babylonian, Hittite, ancient Hebrew, Indian, Chinese, and Japanese literary monuments.

books.title: SENOVĖS EGIPTO POEZIJA
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection of poetry from ancient Egypt, published as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series. It gathers poetic monuments spanning hymns, religious texts, and lyrical works from one of the world's oldest literary traditions. Senoves rytų poezija.

books.title: Senovės Rytų Poezija
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology compiled by Sigitas Geda, collecting ancient Eastern poetry spanning from the 27th–24th centuries BC, including literary monuments from Egyptian, Sumerian, Babylonian, Hittite, ancient Jewish, Indian, Chinese, and Japanese traditions. Published in Vilnius in 1991 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Legenda apie Ulenšpygelį ir Lamę Gudzaką
books.author: Šarlis De Kosteras
books.description: A 19th-century Belgian epic novel following the adventures of Thyl Ulenspiegel and his companion Lamme Goedzak, a spirited Flemish trickster who becomes a hero of resistance against Spanish oppression during the Dutch Revolt. The story blends humor, folklore, and tragedy, with Ulenspiegel embodying the indomitable spirit of Flanders. This is a Lithuanian translation published in Vilnius in 1989.

books.title: ŠVENTASIS RAŠTAS SENASIS TESTAMENTAS 1
books.description: A Lithuanian-language edition of the Old Testament (Senasis Testamentas), translated from Latin (the Vulgate) by Archbishop Juozapas Jonas Skvireckas. Published in Vilnius in 1990 as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series, this is the third edition of Skvireckas's landmark Lithuanian Bible translation.

books.title: Šventasis Raštas: Senasis Testamentas 2
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of the Old Testament (Senasis Testamentas) translated from Latin (Vulgate) by Archbishop Juozapas Jonas Skvireckas, published as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series. This 1991 Vilnius edition is the third republication of Skvireckas's landmark Lithuanian Bible translation.

books.title: Šventasis Raštas 3
books.description: A Lithuanian-language edition of the Old Testament, translated from Latin by Archbishop Juozapas Jonas Skvireckas, published as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series. This 1991 Vilnius edition is the third printing of Skvireckas's landmark Catholic Bible translation.

books.title: Dekameronas
books.author: Džovanis Bokačas
books.description: The Decameron is a 14th-century collection of 100 novellas by Italian author Giovanni Boccaccio, framed around ten young Florentines who flee the Black Death and each tell a story per day over ten days. This is the 1987 Lithuanian-language edition, translated from Italian by Edvardas Viskanta and published in Vilnius.

books.title: DRINOS TILTAS / ANT PROTO RIBOS
books.author: Ivas Andričius / Miroslavas Krleža
books.description: An anthology of two South Slavic novels in Lithuanian translation: Ivo Andrić's Nobel Prize-winning epic chronicling four centuries of Bosnian history through the life of a stone bridge on the Drina River, and Miroslav Krleža's 1938 satirical novel following a middle-aged lawyer whose life unravels after he blurts out an honest thought at a party, exposing the chasm between conformity and individuality.

books.title: Absalomai, Absalomai!
books.author: Viljamas Folkneris
books.description: A Southern Gothic novel tracing the rise and fall of Thomas Sutpen, an ambitious plantation owner in the American South, as recounted by multiple unreliable narrators before, during, and after the Civil War. The novel explores themes of ambition, tragedy, racial legacy, and the elusive nature of historical truth.

books.title: Eilėraščiai. Poemos / Vieno Miesto Istorija
books.author: Nikolajus Nekrasovas / Michailas Saltykovas-Ščedrinas
books.description: An anthology containing poems and narrative verses by 19th-century Russian poet Nikolai Nekrasov, known for his socially conscious portrayals of peasant life, paired with Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin's satirical novel The History of a Town — a grotesque chronicle of the fictional town of Glupov that skewers Russian autocracy and bureaucracy.

books.title: Eilėraščiai Poemos
books.author: Adomas Mickevičius
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection of the most significant lyric poems, ballads, and epic poems by the renowned Polish Romantic poet Adam Mickiewicz, including works such as 'Konradas Valenrodas' and 'Ponas Tadas'. Compiled by Justinas Marcinkevičius and published by Vaga, Vilnius, as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: MOBI DIKAS, ARBA BANGINIS
books.author: Hermanas Melvilis
books.description: An epic tale of the obsessive Captain Ahab and his crew aboard the whaling ship Pequod as they pursue the legendary great white sperm whale across the world's oceans. A sweeping exploration of obsession, revenge, and humanity's place in the universe, widely regarded as one of the greatest American novels ever written.

books.title: Meistras ir Margarita
books.author: Michailas Bulgakovas
books.description: The Devil, posing as Professor Woland, arrives in 1930s Soviet Moscow with his bizarre entourage and wreaks havoc, exposing the moral corruption of Soviet society. The novel weaves together a love story between a struggling writer known as the Master and his devoted Margarita, alongside a reimagined biblical narrative of Pontius Pilate and Yeshua Ha-Nozri.

books.title: Kventinas Dervardas
books.author: Valteris Skotas
books.description: A historical novel set in 15th-century France, following young Scottish archer Quentin Durward as he enters the service of the cunning King Louis XI and becomes entangled in dangerous political intrigue between France and Burgundy. Originally written by Sir Walter Scott and first published in 1823, this is a Lithuanian translation by Juozas Subatavičius.

books.title: Eilėraščiai Poemos Drama
books.author: Tarasas Ševčenka, Ivanas Franko, Lesia Ukrainka
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology published as part of the 'Pasaulinės literatūros bibliotekos' (World Literature Library) series, collecting poems, long-form verse, and drama by three foundational Ukrainian literary figures: Taras Shevchenko, Ivan Franko, and Lesya Ukrainka.

books.title: Dramos Sonetai
books.author: Viljamas Šekspyras
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection of William Shakespeare's plays and sonnets, translated by Aleksys Churginas and published in Vilnius in 1986 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series. It includes major plays such as Richard III, Romeo and Juliet, Hamlet, and Macbeth, alongside Shakespeare's celebrated sonnets.

books.title: ROLANDO GIESMĖ. NIBELUNGŲ GIESMĖ
books.description: This volume contains the most significant French and German medieval heroic epics — the Song of Roland and the Song of the Nibelungs — depicting the battles of knights, their bravery, and heroic deeds. It was published in Vilnius in 1988 as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Tykusis Donas.  1 tomas
books.author: Michailas Šolochovas
books.description: A sweeping four-volume epic following Cossack Grigory Melekhov and his community along the Don River, depicting their lives, loves, and struggles through World War I, the Russian Revolution, and the Civil War. This is Volume I of the Lithuanian translation, published in Vilnius in 1987, translated by Pranas Povilaitis.

books.title: Doriano Grėjaus Portretas / Menininko Jaunų Dienų Portretas
books.author: Oskaras Vaildas / Džeimsas Džoisas
books.description: An anthology of two classic novels in Lithuanian translation: Oscar Wilde's tale of a beautiful young man whose portrait ages in place of him as he descends into moral corruption, and James Joyce's semi-autobiographical coming-of-age story following Stephen Dedalus from childhood through his intellectual and artistic awakening in Ireland.

books.title: SILVESTRO BONARO NUSIKALTIMAS DIEVAI TROKŠTA
books.author: Anatolis Fransas
books.description: A Lithuanian-language volume collecting two novels by Anatole France: *The Crime of Sylvestre Bonnard* (1881), about an aging scholar's obsessive quest for a lost manuscript, and *The Gods Are Athirst* (1912), a historical novel set during the French Revolution's Reign of Terror, following a fanatical young painter who sends countless people to the guillotine before meeting the same fate himself.

books.title: Metamorfozės
books.author: Ovidijus
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Ovid's Metamorphoses, a Latin narrative poem from 8 CE comprising over 250 myths that chronicles the history of the world from its creation to the deification of Julius Caesar. Translated from Latin by Antanas Dambrauskas and published in Vilnius in 1990 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Demonai
books.author: Fiodoras Dostojevskis
books.description: A fictional Russian town descends into chaos as it becomes the focal point of an attempted revolution orchestrated by the conspirator Pyotr Verkhovensky. The novel is Dostoevsky's powerful allegory of the catastrophic consequences of nihilism and radical ideology in 19th-century Russia.

books.title: Tuštybės Mugė   2 Tomas
books.author: Viljamas Meikpisas Tekerėjus
books.description: A panoramic satirical novel set against the backdrop of the Napoleonic Wars, following the contrasting lives of the cunning social climber Becky Sharp and the gentle, naive Amelia Sedley as they navigate the hypocrisies and vanities of early 19th-century English society. This is Volume II of the Lithuanian translation, published in Vilnius in 1990 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series, translated by Stasys Tomonis.

books.title: Saga apie Gestą Berlingą / Nykštukas. Sibilė
books.author: Selma Lagerliof / Peras Lagerkvistas
books.description: This volume contains two works: Selma Lagerlöf's debut novel about Gösta Berling, a defrocked priest who becomes one of the carefree cavaliers at the manor of Ekeby in Sweden's Värmland region; and two novels by Pär Lagerkvist — 'The Dwarf,' a dark Renaissance tale exploring evil, and 'The Sibyl,' about a simple girl chosen as an oracle at Delphi who grapples with questions of earthly love and the divine.

books.title: Apsakymai Dramos
books.author: Maksimas Gorkis
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection of the most significant short stories and plays by Maxim Gorky, founder of socialist realism, depicting a broad panorama of pre-revolutionary Russian folk life. Published in Vilnius in 1988 as part of the 'Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka' (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: NOVELĖS / KARAS SU SALAMANDROMIS
books.author: Žigmondas Moricas / Karelas Čapekas
books.description: This volume contains two works: short stories by Hungarian realist author Zsigmond Móricz, depicting life and social conflicts in rural Hungarian society, and Karel Čapek's 1936 satirical science fiction novel about the discovery of intelligent giant salamanders who are exploited by humans and eventually revolt, serving as a biting allegory for fascism, colonialism, and capitalism.

books.title: Eilėraščiai. Poemos. Pjesės
books.author: Vladimiras Majakovskis
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology collecting the most significant works of Russian Futurist poet Vladimir Mayakovsky, illustrating the evolution of his creative output across genres. Published by Vaga in Vilnius in 1986 as part of the Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Broliai Karamazovai    1 tomas
books.author: Fiodoras Dostojevskis
books.description: Dostoevsky's final masterpiece follows the Karamazov family — a dissolute father and his three sons — through a murder mystery, courtroom drama, and profound philosophical debate. The novel explores themes of faith, free will, morality, and redemption through the contrasting temperaments of brothers Dmitri, Ivan, and Alyosha.

books.title: Eilėraščiai Dramos
books.author: Frydrichas Šileris
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology collecting the most significant poems and dramas of the German literary classic Friedrich Schiller (1759–1805), including plays such as 'Klasta ir meilė' (Intrigue and Love), 'Marija Stiuart' (Mary Stuart), and 'Vilius Telis' (William Tell). Published as volume 32 of the 'Pasaulinės literatūros biblioteka' (World Literature Library) series by Vaga publishing house in Vilnius.

books.title: Mielas draugas. Pjeras ir Žanas. Novelės
books.author: Gi de Mopasanas
books.description: A Lithuanian-language collection featuring two of Guy de Maupassant's novels — Bel-Ami (1885), a satirical portrait of an ambitious journalist's corrupt rise in Parisian society, and Pierre et Jean (1888), a psychological study of two brothers — along with novellas/short stories.

books.title: Quo Vadis
books.author: Henrikas Senkevičius
books.description: Set in ancient Rome during the reign of Emperor Nero, Quo Vadis follows the love story of Marcus Vinicius, a Roman patrician, and Lygia, a young Christian woman, against the backdrop of the brutal persecution of early Christians. The novel explores themes of love, faith, and the clash between paganism and Christianity, and contributed to Sienkiewicz's Nobel Prize in Literature in 1905.

books.title: Raudona ir Juoda
books.author: Stendalis
books.description: A powerful psychological novel set in post-Napoleonic France following Julien Sorel, an ambitious young man of humble origins who uses seduction and cunning to climb the social ladder, navigating the worlds of the church and the aristocracy. It is a sweeping critique of 19th-century French society, exploring themes of ambition, hypocrisy, and the conflict between personal desire and social expectation.

books.title: Tuštybės Mugė
books.author: Viljamas Meikpisas Tekerėjus
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of William Makepeace Thackeray's Vanity Fair (subtitled 'A Novel without a Hero'), following the intertwined lives of the cunning Becky Sharp and the gentle Amelia Sedley amid the social world of early 19th-century England during and after the Napoleonic Wars. This is Volume I, translated by Stasys Tomonis and published in Vilnius in 1990 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Gargantiua ir Pantagriuelis
books.author: Rablė
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of François Rabelais's Renaissance masterpiece, chronicling the fantastical adventures of two giants — Gargantua and his son Pantagruel — blending earthy humor, satire, and philosophical wit to mock human folly and societal norms. Translated from French by Dominykas Urbas and published in Vilnius in 1986 as part of the Pasaulinės Literatūros Biblioteka (World Literature Library) series.

books.title: Broliai Karamazovai      2 tomas
books.author: Fiodoras Dostojevskis
books.description: A sweeping philosophical novel set in 19th-century Russia, following the Karamazov family — a depraved father and his three sons — through a story of patricide, moral struggle, and profound questions about faith, free will, and the existence of God. It is widely considered Dostoevsky's masterpiece and one of the greatest novels in world literature.

books.title: Poezija Drama Proza
books.author: Michailas Lermontovas
books.description: A Lithuanian-language anthology collecting the best works of Russian literary classic Mikhail Lermontov, including his most significant poems, narrative poems, the verse drama Masquerade, and the novel A Hero of Our Time.

books.title: PINIGŲ PADIRBINĖTOJAI
books.author: André Gide
books.description: A complex, polyphonic novel set in Paris intertwining the lives of youths, writers, and schemers to explore authenticity, moral compromise, and the forging of identity. It is a novel-within-a-novel in which a coin counterfeiting ring serves as a metaphor for the broader human tendency toward deception and false values.

books.title: Džudas Nepastebimasis
books.author: Tomas Hardis
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Thomas Hardy's Jude the Obscure, following Jude Fawley, a working-class stonemason who dreams of becoming a scholar, whose ambitions are thwarted by class, an ill-fated marriage, and a tragic love affair with his cousin Sue Bridehead. Published in 1895, Hardy's final novel caused great controversy for its frank critique of Victorian institutions of marriage, religion, and education.

books.title: Daktaras Faustas
books.author: Tomas Manas
books.description: A reimagining of the Faust legend following fictional German composer Adrian Leverkühn, who makes a Faustian pact with the Devil in exchange for musical genius, as narrated by his childhood friend. Set against the backdrop of Germany's descent into fascism, the novel explores themes of art, ambition, and moral decay.

books.title: Sužadėtiniai
books.author: Alesandras Mandzonis
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Alessandro Manzoni's celebrated Italian historical novel *I promessi sposi*, set in 17th-century Spanish-ruled Lombardy, following two peasant lovers whose plans to marry are obstructed by a tyrannical local lord, a cowardly priest, and the upheavals of plague and war. Translated from Italian by Algimantas Vaišnoras and published in Vilnius in 1990 as part of the World Literature Library series.

books.title: Didieji lūkesčiai
books.author: Čarlzas Dikensas
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Charles Dickens's Great Expectations, following the orphan Pip as he rises from humble origins in rural England to pursue wealth and gentility in London. The novel explores themes of social class, ambition, and the discovery that loyalty and compassion matter more than status or fortune.

books.title: Moters Portretas
books.author: Henris Džeimsas
books.description: A Lithuanian translation of Henry James's 1881 novel The Portrait of a Lady, following Isabel Archer, a spirited young American woman who travels to Europe, inherits a fortune, and becomes entangled in Machiavellian scheming that threatens her independence. The novel explores themes of personal freedom, betrayal, and the clash between American and European values.

books.title: Cinko Berniukai
books.author: Svetlana Aleksijevič
books.description: A documentary account of the Soviet-Afghan War told through the voices of soldiers, mothers, and witnesses who experienced its devastating human cost. The title refers to the zinc coffins in which Soviet soldiers were returned home, often in secret.
